<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Here is a sequence of shapes made with grey and white tiles.

![papers/bancrofts-school/2016/sample-paper-2/s02-q01-i00.png](/assets/papers/bancrofts-school/2016/sample-paper-2/s02-q01-i00.png "papers/bancrofts-school/2016/sample-paper-2/s02-q01-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Here is a sequence of shapes made with grey and white tiles.
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>




<ul class="subquestion lower-alpha question_type_subquestion list_type_lower-alpha">
<li class="questionContainer">
<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many grey tiles will be there in Shape Number $20?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many grey tiles will be there in Shape Number $20?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of grey tiles is calculated by adding $1$ to the previous number of grey tiles.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next grey tiles is calculated by adding multiple of $1$ grey tiles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of grey tiles}   &= 3 + (20 - 1) \times 1 \\\\
                              &= 3 + 19 \times 1 \\\\
                              &= 3 + 19 \\\\
                              &= 22
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$22$

**Question**

How many tiles will there be in altogether in Shape Number $25?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many tiles will there be in altogether in Shape Number $25?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of white tiles is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of white tiles.

The number of grey tiles is calculated by adding $1$ to the previous number of grey tiles.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next grey tiles is calculated by adding multiple of $1$ grey tiles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

The next white tiles is calculated by adding multiple of $2$ white tiles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of white tiles}  &= 2 + (25 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                              &= 2 + 24 \times 2 \\\\
                              &= 2 + 48 \\\\
                              &= 50
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of grey tiles}   &= 3 + (25 - 1) \times 1 \\\\
                              &= 3 + 24 \times 1 \\\\
                              &= 3 + 24 \\\\
                              &= 27
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Total Number of tiles}  &= 50 + 27 \\\\
                              &= 77
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$77$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many triangles will there be in the $10  \text{th}$ diagram?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many triangles will there be in the $10  \text{th}$ diagram?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of triangles is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of triangles.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ triangles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of triangles}  &= 1 + (10 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 1 + 9 \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 1 + 18 \\\\
                            &= 19
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$19$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many dots will there be in the $20  \text{th}$ diagram?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many dots will there be in the $20  \text{th}$ diagram?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of dots is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of dots.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ dots to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of dots}       &= 3 + (20 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 3 + 19 \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 3 + 38 \\\\
                            &= 41
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

**Question**

In shape $6$, how many triangles will there be?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

                              &= 11
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Anah makes a shape with $29$ triangles. How many matches did she use?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Anah makes a shape with $29$ triangles. How many matches did she use?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of triangles is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of triangles.

The number of matches is calculated by adding $4$ to the previous number of matches.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $4$ matches and adding multiple of $2$ triangles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

Let the term number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
1 + (a - 1) \times 2    &=  29 \\\\
1 + 2a - 2              &=  29 \\\\
2a - 1                  &=  29 \\\\
2a                      &=  29 + 1 \\\\
2a                      &=  30 \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{30}{2} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{15 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{15 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                       &=  15
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of matches}    &= 3 + (15 - 1) \times 4 \\\\
                            &= 3 + 14 \times 4 \\\\
                            &= 3 + 98 \\\\
                            &= 101 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$101$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many dots will surround the diagram with a row of $20$ squares?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many dots will surround the diagram with a row of $20$ squares?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of dots is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of dots.

The number of squares is equal to the term number.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ dots to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{The term number}      &= \text{number of squares} \\\\ 
                            &= 20
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of dots}   &=  4 + (20 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                        &=  4 + 19 \times 2 \\\\
                        &=  4 + 36 \\\\
                        &=  40 
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$40$

</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many squares are in the diagram which has $148$ dots?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many squares are in the diagram which has $148$ dots?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of dots is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of dots.

The number of squares is equal to the term number.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ dots to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

Let the term number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
4 + (a - 1) \times 2   &= 148 \\\\
4 + 2a - 2             &= 148 \\\\
2a + 2                 &= 148 \\\\
2a                     &= 148 - 2 \\\\
2a                     &= 146 \\\\
a                      &= \dfrac{146}{2} \\\\
a                      &= \dfrac{73 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a                      &= \dfrac{73 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                      &= 73
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}

                            &= 73
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

**Number pattern**

Here is the first part of a number pattern:

$13,  \quad 16,  \quad 19,  \quad 22,  \quad 25,  \quad \ldots$

Which of these numbers will appear somewhere in the pattern?

$36,  \quad 46,  \quad 56,  \quad 100,  \quad 1000$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">**Number pattern**
<emptyline>
Here is the first part of a number pattern:
<emptyline>
$13,  \quad 16,  \quad 19,  \quad 22,  \quad 25,  \quad \ldots$
<emptyline>
Which of these numbers will appear somewhere in the pattern?
<emptyline>
$36,  \quad 46,  \quad 56,  \quad 100,  \quad 1000$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number is calculated by adding $3$ to the previous number.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next number is calculated by adding multiple of $2$ to the first number and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

Let's check with all these numbers

Let the term number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
13 + (a - 1) \times 3   &=  36 \\\\
13 + 3a - 3             &=  36 \\\\
3a + 10                 &=  36 \\\\
3a                      &=  36 - 10 \\\\
3a                      &=  26 \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{26}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  8.66 \text{ (Not possible)}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
13 + (a - 1) \times 3   &=  46 \\\\
13 + 3a - 3             &=  46 \\\\
3a + 10                 &=  46 \\\\
3a                      &=  46 - 10 \\\\
3a                      &=  36 \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{36}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{12 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{12 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
a                       &=  12 \text{ (possible)}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
13 + (a - 1) \times 3   &=  56 \\\\
13 + 3a - 3             &=  56 \\\\
3a + 10                 &=  56 \\\\
3a                      &=  56 - 10 \\\\
3a                      &=  46 \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{46}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  15.33 \text{ (Not possible)}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
13 + (a - 1) \times 3   &=  100 \\\\
13 + 3a - 3             &=  100 \\\\
3a + 10                 &=  100 \\\\
3a                      &=  100 - 10 \\\\
3a                      &=  90 \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{90}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{30 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{30 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
a                       &=  30 \text{ (possible)}
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
13 + (a - 1) \times 3   &=  1000 \\\\
13 + 3a - 3             &=  1000 \\\\
3a + 10                 &=  1000 \\\\
3a                      &=  1000 - 10 \\\\
3a                      &=  990 \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{990}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{330 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a                       &=  \dfrac{330 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
a                       &=  330 \text{ (possible)}
\end{aligned}
$

The numbers will appear are $46$,$100$,$1000$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$46$,$100$,$1000$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the sixth $(6^\text{th})$ term in the sequence?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

**Question**

The first two numbers are $100$ and $102$. What are the next three numbers in the sequence?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The first two numbers are $100$ and $102$. What are the next three numbers in the sequence?
</code></pre>

</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Third number in the sequence}     &= 102 \div 2 \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac{102}{2} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac{51 \times 2}{2} \\\\
                                        &= \dfrac{51 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
                                        &= 51 \\\\
\text{Fourth number in the sequence}    &= 51 + 1 \\\\
                                        &= 52 \\\\
\text{Fifth number in the sequence}     &= 52 \times 2 \\\\
                                        &= 104
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

The $21^\text{st}$ number is $120$ and the $22^\text{nd}$ number is $122$.

What is the $24^\text{th}$ number?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>

                                        &= 62
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Naheeda uses $10$ matchsticks to make a row of $3$ squares.
How many matchsticks would she need to make a row of $7$ squares?

![papers/forest-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q09-i00.png](/assets/papers/forest-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q09-i00.png "papers/forest-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s01-q09-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Naheeda uses $10$ matchsticks to make a row of $3$ squares.
How many matchsticks would she need to make a row of $7$ squares?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="tip">

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

As shown in the figure,

To make a row of $n$ squares, we need $3n + 1$ matchsticks.

So,

For making a row of 7 squares

$
\begin{aligned}
&= 3 \times 7 + 1 \\\\
&= 21 + 1 \\\\
&= 22
\end{aligned}
$

She need $22$ matchsticks for making a row of 7 squares.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$22$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The first term of the sequence is $50$, the second is $46$ and the third is $42$, and so on.
How many terms are there until the first negative term?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The first term of the sequence is $50$, the second is $46$ and the third is $42$, and so on.
How many terms are there until the first negative term?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The next term is calculated by subtracting $4$ from the previous term. Hence, the sequence would be:

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(-4)}}  \\
50,  &&    46,  &&  42,  &&   38,  &&   34, &&  30, && 26, && 22, && 18, && 14, && 10, && 6, && 2, && -2
\end{matrix}
$

By counting these terms we get,

$13$ terms are required to reach the first negative term.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$13$

</div>
</div>
<div class="workingscodeblock">
<div class="tipcodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">- rtq_abbr_note_md_sequence_find_difference

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

This $5$ by $5$ square is made up of a row of white squares, then a row of white and black squares,  then a row of white squares and so on. 

There are $4$ black squares.  How many black squares would there be in a $7$ by $7$ square coloured in the same way?

|:------------------:|:--:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:----:|

<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Complete the table below, to show how many matches there are.
<emptyline>
| Number of squares | $1$ | $3$ | $5$ | $6$ | $7$ | $20$ |
|:------------------:|:--:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:----:|
| Number of matches | $4$ | $10$ |  |  |  |  |
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of matches is calculated by adding $3$ to the number of matches required for the previous number of squares.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $3$ matches to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

| Number of squares | $1$ | $3$  | $5$           | $6$           | $7$           | $20$                          |
|-------------------|-----|------|---------------|---------------|---------------|-------------------------------|
| Number of matches | $4$ | $10$ | $10 + 3 + 3 = 16$ | $16 + 3 = 19$ | $19 + 3 = 22$ | $4 + (20 - 1) \times 3 =  61$ |
</div>

**Question**

How many black squares will there be in the $8^{th}$ pattern?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many black squares will there be in the $8^{th}$ pattern?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of black squares} &= \dfrac{8}{2} \times 3 \\\\
                               &= \dfrac{4 \times 2}{2} \times 3 \\\\
                               &= \dfrac{4 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \times 3 \\\\
                               &= 4 \times 3 \\\\
                               &= 12 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

How many squares will there be in total in the $19^{th}$ pattern?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many squares will there be in total in the $19^{th}$ pattern?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of squares is calculated by adding $3$ to the previous number of squares.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $3$ squares to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of squares in } 19^\text{th} \text{ pattern}   &= 1 + (19 - 1) \times 3 \\\\
                                                            &= 1 + 18 \times 3 \\\\
                                                            &= 1 + 54 \\\\
                                                            &= 55 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$55$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Which pattern number has $31$ white squares and $33$ black squares?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Which pattern number has $31$ white squares and $33$ black squares?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the term number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
1 + \dfrac{(a - 1)}{2} \times 3 &= 31 \\\\
\dfrac{(a - 1)}{2} \times 3     &= 31 - 1 \\\\
\dfrac{(a - 1)}{2} \times 3     &= 30 \\\\
\dfrac{(a - 1)}{2}              &= \dfrac{30}{3} \\\\
\dfrac{(a - 1)}{2}              &= \dfrac{3 \times 10}{3} \\\\
\dfrac{(a - 1)}{2}              &= \dfrac{\cancel{3} \times 10}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
\dfrac{(a - 1)}{2}              &= 10 \\\\
a - 1                           &= 10 \times 2 \\\\
a - 1                           &= 20 \\\\
a                               &= 21
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
0 + \dfrac{a}{2} \times 3    &= 33 \\\\
\dfrac{a}{2}                 &= \dfrac{33}{3} \\\\
\dfrac{a}{2}                 &= \dfrac{11 \times 3}{3} \\\\
\dfrac{a}{2}                 &= \dfrac{11 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
\dfrac{a}{2}                 &= 11 \\\\
a                            &= 11 \times 2 \\\\
a                            &= 22
\end{aligned}
$

$22^\text{nd}$ pattern number has $31$ white squares and $33$ black squares.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$22$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

How many coloured squares are needed when $6$ white squares are used? 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many coloured squares are needed when $6$ white squares are used? 
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of coloured squares is calculated by adding $3$ to previous number of coloured squares.

The number of white squares is equal to the term number.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $3$ coloured squares to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

The term number $= 6$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of coloured squares}   &= 4 + (6 - 1) \times 3 \\\\
                                    &= 4 + 5 \times 3 \\\\
                                    &= 4 + 15 \\\\
                                    &= 19
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$19$

</div>
</div>

![papers/leicester-high-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-3/s01-q20-s02-i00.png](/assets/papers/leicester-high-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-3/s01-q20-s02-i00.png "papers/leicester-high-school-for-girls/sample/sample-paper-3/s01-q20-s02-i00.png")

Twenty coloured squares are used in Pattern $B$. How many white squares are needed?

</div>

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of coloured squares is calculated by adding $2$ to previous number of coloured squares.

The number of white squares is equal to the term number.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ coloured squares to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

Let the term number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
4 + (a - 1) \times 2       &= 20 \\\\
4 + 2a - 2                 &= 20 \\\\
2a + 2                     &= 20 \\\\
2a                         &= 20 - 2 \\\\
2a                         &= 18 \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac{18}{2} \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac{9 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a                          &= \dfrac{9 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                          &= 9
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of white squares}   &= a \\\\
                                 &= 9 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$9$

As it turns, a pattern is left on the ground.

$Y \ R \ G  \ Y  \ R \dots$

**Working**

The next term is calculated by multiplying the previous term by $\dfrac{x}{3}$. Hence, the sequence would be:

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize{\maroonC { (\times \dfrac{x}{3})} }   
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC { (\times \dfrac{x}{3})} }
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC { (\times \dfrac{x}{3})} }
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC { (\times \dfrac{x}{3})} } 
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC { (\times \dfrac{x}{3})} }   
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC { (\times \dfrac{x}{3})} } \\
x,  &&  \dfrac{x^2}{3},  &&  \dfrac{x^3}{9},  &&   \dfrac{x^4}{27},  &&   \dfrac{x^5}{81},  &&  \ldots,  &&  \ldots
\end{matrix}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First missing number}     &= \dfrac{x^5}{81} \times \dfrac{x}{3} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac{x^5 \times x}{81 \times 3} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac{x^6}{243} \\\\
\text{Second missing number}    &= \dfrac{x^6}{243} \times \dfrac{x}{3} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac{x^6 \times x}{243 \times 3} \\\\
                                &= \dfrac{x^7}{729}
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

|:--------------:|:------------------------------------:|

| $7$            | $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 = 28$     |
| $8$            | $1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 + 7 + 8 = 36$ |

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The next term is calculated by adding $4$ to the previous term. Hence, the sequence would be:

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+4)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+4)}}  \\
3,  &&    7,  &&  11,  &&   15,  &&   19,  && \ldots,  && \ldots, && \ldots
\end{matrix}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {First missing number}    &= 19 + 4 \\\\
                                &= 23 \\\\
\text {Second missing number}   &= 23 + 4 \\\\
                                &= 27 \\\\
\text {Third missing number}    &= 27 + 4 \\\\
                                &= 31
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of rectangles is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of rectangles.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ rectangles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of rectangles} &= 4 + (5 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 4 + 4 \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 4 + 8 \\\\
                            &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$12$

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The number of rectangles is calculated by adding $2$ to the previous number of rectangles.
<emptyline>
This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.
<emptyline>
The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ rectangles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of rectangles} &= 4 + (10 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 4 + 9 \times 2 \\\\
                            &= 4 + 18 \\\\
                            &= 22
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>
</div>
</div>

**Question**

How many rectangles would there be in a pattern with $34$ 
triangles?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many rectangles would there be in a pattern with $34$ 
triangles?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the number of rectangles $= a$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
4 + (a-1) \times 2   &= 34 \\\\
4 + 2a - 2           &= 34 \\\\
4 - 2 + 2a           &= 34 \\\\
2 + 2a               &= 34 \\\\
2a                   &= 34 - 2 \\\\
2a                   &= 32 \\\\
a                    &= \dfrac{32}{2} \\\\
a                    &= \dfrac{16 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a                    &= \dfrac{16 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                    &= 16
\end{aligned}
$

Number of rectangles $= 16$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the first missing number $= a$

and the second missing number $= b$

As per the question, 

Let's find $a$ first

$
\begin{aligned}
-23 + a     &= 35 \\\\
a           &= 35 + 23 \\\\
a           &= 58
\end{aligned}
$

Now let's find $b$

$
\begin{aligned}
\dfrac{35}{b}       &= 70 \\\\
\dfrac{35}{70}      &= b \\\\
b                   &= \dfrac{35}{70} \\\\
b                   &= \dfrac{35}{35 \times 2} \\\\
b                   &= \dfrac{\cancel{35}}{\cancel{35} \times 2} \\\\
b                   &= \dfrac{1}{2} \\\\
b                   &= 0.5
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First missing number}   &= a \\\\
                              &= 58 \\\\
\text{Second missing number}  &= b \\\\
                              &= 0.5
\end{aligned}
$

$E_{4}$ means 'add up the first $4$ even numbers', so $E_{4} = 2 + 4 + 6 + 8 = 20$ and so on.

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Here is part of a number sequence. The numbers increase by the same amount each time.

$150 \quad 165 \quad 180 \quad 195 \quad 210$

The sequence continues. 

Circle all of the numbers below that would appear in the sequence:

$315 \quad 561 \quad 240 \quad 620 \quad 964$

$

&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+15)}}

&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+15)}}  \\

\end{matrix}
$

So, we can say that, the numbers that would appear in the sequence are multiples of $15$ .

Numbers that are divisible by $15$ and would appear in the sequence are $=240, 315$

**Question**

A number of shapes have been made with matches.

For this pattern:

![papers/streatham-and-clapham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s02-q03-i00.png](/assets/papers/streatham-and-clapham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s02-q03-i00.png "papers/streatham-and-clapham-high-school/sample/sample-paper-1/s02-q03-i00.png")

How many matches will be in the $4^\text{th}$ shape?

- $26$
- $18$  
- $24$   
- $20$  
- $22$  

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

- $20$  
- $22$  
</code></pre>

                        &= 10 + 36 \\\\

$

**Question**

A sequence of numbers which go up (or down) by a fixed amount each time is called an **arithmetic progression $(AP)$**. For example, the sequence 

$1 ^\text{st}$ term $= 5.8, 2 ^\text{nd}$ term $= 6.0,  3 ^\text{rd}$ term $= 6.2, 4 ^\text{th}$ term = $6.4$ 

is an $AP$ because the terms go up by $0.2$ every time.

</div>

<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</div>

**Question**

The $1 ^\text{st}$ term of an $AP$ is $9$ and the $3 ^\text{rd}$ term is $15$. Work out the $2 ^\text{nd}$ term. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The $1 ^\text{st}$ term of an $AP$ is $9$ and the $3 ^\text{rd}$ term is $15$. Work out the $2 ^\text{nd}$ term. 
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the difference $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
9 + 2d                          &= 15 \\\\
2d                              &= 15 - 9 \\\\
2d                              &= 6 \\\\
d                               &= \dfrac{6}{2} \\\\
d                               &= \dfrac{3 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
d                               &= 3 \\\\
2 \ \text {th number}           &= 9 + 3 \\\\
                                &= 12
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>

<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The $1 ^\text{st}$ term of an $AP$ is $5.8$ and the $2 ^\text{nd}$ term is $5.9$. Work out the $100 ^\text{th}$ term. 

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The $1 ^\text{st}$ term of an $AP$ is $5.8$ and the $2 ^\text{nd}$ term is $5.9$. Work out the $100 ^\text{th}$ term. 
</code></pre>
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the difference $= d$

As per the question,

$
\begin{aligned}
5.8 + d                         &= 5.9 \\\\
d                               &= 5.9 - 5.8 \\\\
d                               &= 0.1 \\\\
100 \ \text {th number}         &= 5.8 + 0.1 \times 99 \\\\
                                &= 5.8 + 9.9 \\\\
                                &= 15.7
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

The next term is calculated by adding $3$ to the previous term. Hence, the sequence would be:

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+3)}}
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(+3)}}

\end{matrix}
$

\begin{aligned}

\text{Second missing number}   &= 19 + 3 \\\\
                               &= 22
\end{aligned}
$

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the largest number in the pattern which is less than $40?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the largest number in the pattern which is less than $40?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the term number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
1 + (a - 1) \times 3     &<    40 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 3         &<    40 - 1 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 3         &<    39 \\\\
a - 1                    &<    \dfrac{39}{3} \\\\
a - 1                    &<    \dfrac{13 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a - 1                    &<    \dfrac{13 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
a - 1                    &<    13 \\\\
a                        &<    13 + 1 \\\\
a                        &<    14
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Largest number} &= 1 + (13-1) \times 3 \\\\
                      &= 1 + 12 \times 3 \\\\
                      &= 1 + 36 \\\\
                      &= 37
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$37$

</div>
</div>

**Working**

The next term is calculated by adding $4$ to the previous term. Hence, the sequence would be:

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+4)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+4)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+4)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+4)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+4)} }

&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+4)} } \\
3,  &&    7,  &&  11,  &&   15,  &&   19,   &&   23,  &&  27,  && \ldots,  && \ldots
\end{matrix}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text {First missing number}   &= 27 + 4 \\\\
                               &= 31 \\\\
\text {Second missing number}  &= 31 + 4 \\\\
                               &= 35
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

What is the first number in the pattern which is greater than $48?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">What is the first number in the pattern which is greater than $48?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the term number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
3 + (a - 1) \times 4     &>    48 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 4         &>    48 - 3 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 4         &>    45 \\\\
a - 1                    &>    \dfrac{45}{4} \\\\
a - 1                    &>    11.25 \\\\
a                        &>    11.25 + 1 \\\\
a                        &>    12.25 \\\\
a                        &\approx  13
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First number greater than } 48      &= 3 + (13-1) \times 4 \\\\
                                          &= 3 + 12 \times 4 \\\\
                                          &= 3 + 48 \\\\
                                          &= 51
\end{aligned}
$

$51$ is the first number in the pattern which is greater than $48$.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$51$

</div>
</div>

Which pattern number is it?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">There is a pattern with $40$ white tiles.
<emptyline>
Which pattern number is it?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the pattern number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
8 + (a - 1) \times 4   &= 40 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 4       &= 40 - 8 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 4       &= 32 \\\\
a - 1                  &= \dfrac{32}{4} \\\\
a - 1                  &= \dfrac{\cancel{4} \times 8}{\cancel{4}} \\\\
a - 1                  &= 8 \\\\
a                      &= 8 + 1 \\\\
a                      &= 9 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

Pattern number $= 9$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$9$

| Number    |         Sum                                           | Multiple of $9$

|  $2007$   | $2 + 0 + 0 + 7 = \green {9}$                          |  Yes
|  $163$    | $1 + 6 + 3 = \red {10}$                               |  No
|  $918$    | $9 + 1 + 8 = \green {18}$                             |  Yes
|  $45$     | $4 + 5 = \green {9}$                                  |  Yes

Answer $= 2007, \ 918, \ 45$
</div>

**Question**

How many white squares would be needed for a pattern with $9$ dark squares?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many white squares would be needed for a pattern with $9$ dark squares?
</code></pre>

<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

%empty%
</div>
</div>

%empty%
</div>

<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Pattern number = 9

$
\begin{aligned}

                                 &= 5 + 8 \times 2 \\\\
                                 &= 5 + 16 \\\\
                                 &= 21
\end{aligned}
$
</div>

<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$21$

**Question**

How many dark squares would be needed for a pattern with $23$ white squares?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many dark squares would be needed for a pattern with $23$ white squares?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the pattern number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
5 + (a - 1) \times 2   &= 23 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 2       &= 23 - 5 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 2       &= 18 \\\\
a - 1                  &= \dfrac{18}{2} \\\\
a - 1                  &= \dfrac{9 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a - 1                  &= \dfrac{9 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a - 1                  &= 9 \\\\
a                      &= 9 + 1 \\\\
a                      &= 10 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of dark squares}  &= a \\\\
                               &= 10 \\\\
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$10$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question_envelope rag_not_found subquestion">
<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

A pattern has $45$ squares in total. How many of them are white?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">A pattern has $45$ squares in total. How many of them are white?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the pattern number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
a + 5 + (a - 1) \times 2    &=  45 \\\\
a + 5 + 2a - 2              &=  45 \\\\
a + 2a + 5 - 2              &=  45 \\\\
3a + 3                      &=  45 \\\\
3a                          &=  45 - 3 \\\\
3a                          &=  42 \\\\
a                           &=  \dfrac{42}{3} \\\\
a                           &=  \dfrac{14 \times 3}{3} \\\\
a                           &=  \dfrac{14 \times \cancel{3}}{\cancel{3}} \\\\
a                           &=  14 
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of white squares}    &= 5 + (a - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                                  &= 5 + (14 - 1) \times 2 \\\\
                                  &= 5 + 13 \times 2 \\\\
                                  &= 5 + 26 \\\\
                                  &= 31
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$31$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

Here is a sequence of whole numbers.

$7  \quad 22  \quad 11  \quad 34  \quad 17$

The rule for the next number in the sequence is:

- if the last number is odd then multiply it by $3$ and add $1$ 
- if the last number is even then halve it.

In the following sequence the first three numbers have been left out. 
Fill in the numbers to show three different possible sequences which obey the rule above.

$

\boxed{\phantom{16}} \quad
16 \quad 8  \quad 4  \quad 2  \quad 1  \quad 4$

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

The second pattern has four small squares and is made from six lines. 

How many lines are needed to draw $64$ small squares?

![papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q33-i00.png](/assets/papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q33-i00.png "papers/the-london-independent-girls-schools-consortium/2009/group-2/s01-q33-i00.png")

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The second pattern has four small squares and is made from six lines. 
<emptyline>
How many lines are needed to draw $64$ small squares?
<emptyline>
%image%
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

Let the pattern number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
a^2                     &= 64 \\\\
a                       &= \sqrt{64} \\\\
a                       &= 8 \\\\
\text{Number of lines}  &= (8 + 1) \times 2 \\\\
                        &= 9 \times 2 \\\\
                        &= 18
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$18$

</div>
</div>

**Question**

How many black hexagons are there in pattern number $13?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">How many black hexagons are there in pattern number $13?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">

<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of black hexagons is calculated by adding $1$ to the previous number of black hexagons.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $1$ black hexagons to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of black hexagons}    &= 2 + (13 - 1) \times 1 \\\\
                                   &= 2 + 12 \times 1 \\\\
                                   &= 2 + 12 \\\\
                                   &= 14
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$14$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question subquestion" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

One pattern has $50$ white hexagons.

How many black hexagons are there in this pattern?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">One pattern has $50$ white hexagons.
<emptyline>
How many black hexagons are there in this pattern?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $2$ white hexagons and adding multiple of $1$ black hexagons to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

Let the pattern number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
8 + (a - 1) \times 2         &= 50 \\\\
8 + 2a - 2                   &= 50 \\\\
6 + 2a                       &= 50 \\\\
2a                           &= 50 - 6 \\\\
2a                           &= 44 \\\\
a                            &= \dfrac{44}{2} \\\\
a                            &= \dfrac{22 \times 2}{2} \\\\
a                            &= \dfrac{22 \times \cancel{2}}{\cancel{2}} \\\\
a                            &= 22
\end{aligned}
$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of white hexagons}      &= 2 + (22 - 1) \times 1 \\\\
                                     &= 2 + 21 \times 1 \\\\
                                     &= 2 + 21 \\\\
                                     &= 23
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$23$

</div>
</div>

2a                           &= 50 - 6 \\\\

a                            &= \dfrac{44}{2} \\\\

**Working**

The number of circles is calculated by adding $4$ to the previous number of circles.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $4$ circles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of circles}  &= 1 + (6 -  1) \times 4 \\\\
                          &= 1 + 5 \times 4 \\\\
                          &= 1 + 20 \\\\
                          &= 21
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Which pattern has $37$ circles?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">

</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">

</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of circles is calculated by adding $4$ to the previous number of circles.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $4$ circles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

Let the pattern number $= a$

$
\begin{aligned}
1 + (a - 1) \times 4    &= 37 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 4        &= 37 - 1 \\\\
(a - 1) \times 4        &= 36 \\\\
a - 1                   &= \dfrac{36}{4} \\\\
a - 1                   &= \dfrac{\cancel{4} \times 9}{\cancel{4}} \\\\
a - 1                   &= 9 \\\\
a                       &= 9 + 1 \\\\
a                       &= 10
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

$10$

<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">The number of circles is calculated by adding $4$ to the previous number of circles.
<emptyline>
This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.
<emptyline>
The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $4$ circles to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.
<emptyline>
Let the pattern number $= a$
<emptyline>
$
\begin{aligned}
1 + (a - 1) \times 4    &= 100 \\\\
1 + 4a - 4              &= 100 \\\\
4a - 3                  &= 100 \\\\
4a                      &= 100 + 3 \\\\
4a                      &= 103 \\\\
a                       &= \dfrac{103}{4} \\\\
a                       &= 25.75 \text{ (Not possible)}
\end{aligned}
$
</code></pre>

**Question**

Pattern $3$ will contain a third ring of hexagons.

How many hexagons will there be **altogether** in pattern $3?$

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Pattern $3$ will contain a third ring of hexagons.
<emptyline>
How many hexagons will there be **altogether** in pattern $3?$
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

The number of hexagons is calculated by adding $6$ to the previous number of hexagons.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next pattern is made by adding multiple of $6$ hexagons to the first pattern and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{Number of hexagons}     &= 1 + (3 - 1) \times 6 \\\\
                              &= 1 + 2 \times 6 \\\\
                              &= 1 + 12 \\\\
                              &= 13
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$13$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

If the differences between each pair of consecutive terms of a sequence are taken, and then the differences in this new sequence are taken, and so on, the numbers may turn out to be the same.

$
\begin{aligned}
& \text{For example for the sequence:}   &&   1   &&  &&   4   &&   &&   9   && && 16 && && 25 \\
& \text{The first differences are:}      &&   &&  3   &&   &&  5    &&   &&7  && && 9          \\ 
& \text{And the second differences are:} &&   &&  &&  2    &&  &&   2 && && 2
\end{aligned}
$

As the second differences are the same, we say that the original sequence is a ''sequence of order $\bold {2}$''

</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

Brian starts with $1000$ and subtracts $11$ each time. The first four numbers in his sequence are:

$1000,\quad 989,\quad 978,\quad 967$


If he continues in this way, what will be the first negative number in his sequence?

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">Brian starts with $1000$ and subtracts $11$ each time. The first four numbers in his sequence are:
<emptyline>
$1000,\quad 989,\quad 978,\quad 967$
<emptyline>

If he continues in this way, what will be the first negative number in his sequence?
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize{\maroonC{(1000-11 \times 1)}}  
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(1000-11 \times 2)}}    
&&  \footnotesize{\maroonC{(1000-11 \times 3)}} \\
1000,  &&    989,  &&  978,  &&   967 \ldots
\end{matrix}
$

The next term is calculated by subtracting $11$ from the previous term.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next term is calculated by subtracting multiple of $11$ to the first term and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

Let the first negative number in the sequence be $1000 - 11a$

$
\begin{aligned}
1000 - 11a              &< 0 \\\\
1000                    &< 11a \\\\
11a                     &> 1000 \\\\
a                       &> \dfrac{1000}{11} \\\\
a                       &> 90.90 \\\\
a                       &\approx 91 
\end{aligned}
$

The first negative number in the sequence = $1000 - 11a$

$
\begin{aligned}
\text{First negative number}    &= 1000 - 11 \times a \\\\
                                &= 1000 - 11 \times 91 \\\\
                                &= 1000 - 1001 \\\\
                                &= -1
\end{aligned}
$
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

$-1$

</div>
</div>

<div class="question" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Question**

This sequence of numbers goes up by $30$ each time.

$30,\quad 60,\quad 90,\quad 120,\quad 150,\quad \ldots$

The sequence continues.

Will the number $1330$ be in the sequence? 

Explain how you know:

</div>
<div class="questioncodeblock" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">
<div class="questioncodeblock_title">
<strong style="display: block; margin-bottom: 0.5rem;">Question Raw</strong>
</div>
<pre class="language-latex"><code class="language-latex">This sequence of numbers goes up by $30$ each time.
<emptyline>
$30,\quad 60,\quad 90,\quad 120,\quad 150,\quad \ldots$
<emptyline>
The sequence continues.
<emptyline>
Will the number $1330$ be in the sequence? 
<emptyline>
Explain how you know:
</code></pre>
</div>
<div class="workings">
<div class="tips" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Tips**

<div class="tip">
- ABBR:  Let's find the relation between the consecutive terms of the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="formulas placeholder" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Formulas**

<div class="formula">
%empty%
</div>
</div>
<div class="working" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Working**

$
\begin{matrix}
&   \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+30)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+30)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+30)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+30)} }
&&  \footnotesize {\maroonC {(+30)} }  \\
30,  &&    60,  &&  90,  &&   120,  &&  150,  && \ldots
\end{matrix}
$

The next term is calculated by adding $30$ to the previous term.

This is an arithmetic sequence too and the difference between the consecutive patterns of the sequence is constant.

The next term is calculated by adding multiple of $30$ to the first term and the number of times it is added is based on the position in the sequence.

Let the number of term $= n$

$
\begin{aligned}
30 + 30 \times (n - 1)  &= 1330 \\\\
30 + 30n - 30           &= 1330 \\\\
30n                     &= 1330 \\\\
n                       &= \dfrac {1330} {30} \\\\
n                       &= \dfrac {133 \cancel {0}} {3 \cancel {0}} \\\\
n                       &= \dfrac {133} {3} \\\\
n                       &= 44 \dfrac {1} {3}
\end{aligned}
$

$44 \dfrac {1} {3}$ is not a whole number.

Hence, the number $1330$ will not be in the sequence.
</div>
</div>
<div class="answers">
<div class="answer" style="margin: 1rem 0; padding: 0.85rem 1rem; border: 1px solid #9ea7b3; border-radius: 6px;">

**Answer**

No

</div>
</div>
